claim.title: Exact finite-sample bias-variance decomposition (Lemma 1)
claim.statement: For n<=d and beta_hat=X^dagger y, the bias is B_n=||E_X[Proj_{X^perp}(beta)]||^2 and the variance is V_n=E_X[||Proj_X(beta)-E_X[Proj_X(beta)]||^2] + sigma^2 E_X[Tr((XX^T)^{-1})].
claim.test_plan: For several n<d (e.g., d=1000, n=100,300,500,700,900), generate many independent X matrices and noise vectors eta. Compute beta_hat=X^T(XX^T)^{-1}(X beta+eta). Compute the Monte-Carlo empirical bias and variance. Independently compute the right-hand side using the same samples: the orthogonal projector onto the rowspace of X and Tr((XX^T)^{-1}).
claim.success_criterion: The Monte-Carlo estimates of B_n and V_n agree with the right-hand side expressions within 5% relative error (or within Monte Carlo standard error).
